summary: Batched session replay token invalidation causing 403s for private import jobs
description: Issue summary: DatumHealth reports intermittent 403 Authorization failures for a set of scheduled bulk 'dataset import' jobs running in their private VPC deployment. Failures are transient and correlate with high parallelism when multiple import workers start within the same 30s window. Impact: Several hundred import tasks failed intermittently over the last 24 hours, blocking data onboarding pipelines. Environment: private deployment (DatumHealth), prod-us-east, Redwood Private v2026.02.x, identity-proxy behind customer ingress, Redis session-store managed in customer VPC. Expected: Batched import workers should receive valid session tokens and complete without authorization errors. Actual: ~12-18% of batched worker attempts receive 403 from admin-console/auth-check and are retried by DatumHealth job orchestrator, causing delays and some job-level failures. Customer first reported 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer runs dataset-import with 48 parallel workers using the same service-account API key via admin-console REST endpoint.
2) Each worker requests a short-lived session token from identity-proxy (assertion exchange), then calls Redwood admin API to start an import session.
3) When the worker pool starts within a tight window (<30s), ~15% of workers receive 403 responses from the admin API immediately after token exchange.
4) Reducing parallelism to <8 workers eliminates the failures.
5) Reproduced locally against customer private cluster with load generator reproducing 48 concurrent assertions; same 403 pattern observed intermittently.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token signature/audience mismatch — ruled out by signature validation logs and consistent client assertion aud fields.

Observed correlation between high parallel assertion traffic and Redis 'key not found' on token validation path. Key TTLs are short (60s) but failures occur immediately after creation, suggesting a write/read race or eviction event.
Redis metrics (customer-provided) show 'maxmemory' reached spikes during burst: eviction_policy configured as 'volatile-lru' and average memory usage peaked at 96% during import window.

identity-proxy writes tokens as single shared session key per service-account assertion fingerprint. Multiple workers exchanging the same assertion concurrently caused rapid overwrites of the session key (last-write wins) and version mismatch on admin-console validation.
Trace analysis: several tokens created with same session_fingerprint but different token_id; admin-console validated a token_id that had been overwritten/evicted milliseconds earlier (race).
Attached linked GitHub PR contains a proposed fix to write a versioned session metadata object and use CAS-style compare-and-set on session-store key updates (PR #2789).
Customer cluster suggested workaround: increase Redis memory and switch eviction_policy to 'noeviction' for session namespace, OR stagger worker startup to avoid concurrent assertions.
resolution: Mitigation steps applied 2026-03-12: 1) Deployed identity-proxy v2026.03.12 to customer private control plane which implements versioned session keys and optimistic compare-and-set to prevent last-write invalidation under concurrent exchanges (PR #2789). 2) Recommended Redis config changes: increase memory + set eviction_policy to noeviction for session namespace. 3) Supported DatumHealth to stagger worker startup as temporary workaround. Post-deploy observation: import worker parallelism at 48 now completes with <0.5% transient auth failures (noise floor) and subsequent fixes planned to remove residual flakiness. Follow-up: engineering will schedule a longer-term test harness for high-concurrency assertion storm scenarios and add an alert when session-store memory >85% during bursts. Ticket will be closed after 72h of clean runs; customer confirmed reduced job failures in last 24h.
